note: Cases CLAUDE.md invariant 7 and registry-oracle-notes.md §11 name as the known ways to be confidently wrong. Each defeated some plausible parser. The last two cases assert STRUCTURE (were the keys found at all) rather than required/raw sets: those would have to be filled from the parser's own output, and a fixture that copies the parser cannot test it. Their key counts come from counting `new KeyedCodec` in the file independently.

cases.label: raw KeyedCodec + true THIRD ARGUMENT = required
cases.why: `new KeyedCodec("Shapes", new MapCodec<...>(...), true)` - raw, so a pattern expecting KeyedCodec<T> skips it and undercounts; and required by the third argument, so stopping at the first balanced paren keeps the key but loses its requiredness. Its four keys include exactly one required.

cases.label: raw KeyedCodec + true INSIDE the inner constructor = NOT required
cases.why: Same key NAME `Shapes`, also raw, but `new KeyedCodec("Shapes", new SetCodec<...>(..., true))` - two arguments, the true inside the inner constructor. Attributing it to the outer codec manufactures a requirement, and invariant 7 calls that the dangerous direction: a fabricated *required* can never be contradicted by a shipped asset.

cases.label: requiredness by Validators.nonNull() attached AFTER append(...) closes
cases.why: CLAUDE.md: `Name` is the sole key carrying Validators.nonNull(). Parsing to the first balanced paren reports NO required keys at all, because the validator attaches on the builder two calls further along, before .add().

cases.label: same simple name, different file, different key and requiredness
cases.why: The twin of the `StartObjective` interaction in the 44. Both declare exactly ONE key, so a count cross-check agrees while the key name and its requiredness are both wrong: this one is `ObjectiveId`, not required; the registered interaction is `Setup`, required.

cases.label: chain on a *_BUILDER field, .build()-ed into the public codec
cases.why: Item.CODEC is `CODEC_BUILDER.build()`. Scanning the CODEC statement alone returns ZERO keys and the appends==adds==keys self-check ENDORSES it — on the corpus's most-documented asset type (items.md plus five items-*.md pages). One key, `State`, is appended to the builder ~700 lines BELOW the declaration, so following the field is necessary but not sufficient; the scan must also collect appends on that field elsewhere in the file.

cases.label: .addField(...) declares keys too
cases.why: Matching only .append/.appendInherited misses .addField — 273 uses across 41 classes in build-26. This class declares all 8 of its keys that way and parsed as zero with the self-check green.

cases.label: BuilderCodec.abstractBuilder puts the PARENT in argument ONE
cases.why: `BuilderCodec.builder(X.class, X::new, Parent.CODEC)` puts the parent third; `BuilderCodec.abstractBuilder(X.class, Parent.CODEC)` puts it SECOND, and a parser reading args[2] records no parent at all. 96 chains in build-26 use abstractBuilder against 1516 plain builders, so it looks negligible and is not: every one of them is a BASE class, which is precisely what other chains inherit from. Found by auditing why 15 inherited-scope bindings were rejected on `Next` — a key SimpleInteraction declares and the walk could not reach, because the link was severed at the first abstract base.
